verdict: Microchip's sales surged 42% to $1.6B as the long chip downturn ended, and GAAP profit jumped from $42M to $401M as margins snapped back.

kpis.label: Dividends paid
kpis.note: returned to common stockholders in the quarter

segments.name: Semiconductor products
segments.note: Microcontrollers, analog chips and connectivity products sold into industrial, data center, automotive, aerospace and consumer products. Microchip reports as a single segment; growth was led by industrial and data center demand.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing the next microcontrollers and analog chips.

opex.name: Amortization of acquired intangibles
opex.note: Accounting write-down of technology bought in past acquisitions — a non-cash charge excluded from non-GAAP results.

otherDetail: Mostly interest expense on Microchip's debt, net of interest income.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The downturn is over
takeaways.text: Sales rose 42% year over year and 9% sequentially, above the high end of guidance, with bookings strong and the book-to-bill ratio well above one — orders exceed shipments.

takeaways.title: Margins snapped back
takeaways.text: Gross margin recovered to 65.9% from 55.9% a year ago as factories refilled, turning the sales rebound into a fivefold jump in operating income to $464M.

takeaways.title: Data center design wins doubled
takeaways.text: Microchip's PCIe Gen 6 switch and retimer design wins for AI data centers reached 24, up from 12 a quarter earlier; it also closed the Hailo edge-AI acquisition in September.

footerNote: Figures are rounded to whole $M from the release's one-decimal presentation ($1,621.5M of net sales), so minor rounding differences may occur. Net income of $401M is before $28M of dividends on Series A preferred stock; $374M was attributable to common stockholders. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.97, excluding amortization and special items.
